text:
maya: Quick check — I'm kicking off the pricing rollout for the new compute tiers tomorrow. We ran the A/B buckets, results look good, but need signoff on two things before we flip: 1) grandfathering rules (who gets preserved legacy rates) and 2) vendor pass-through rates — some committed discounts from our infra vendor changed last week. attaching the draft cohort mapping: https://drive.redwood/pricing/cohort-map-2026.csv

sam: Thanks, maya. Can you paste the current cohort rules here? I want to confirm the exact cutoff for grandfathering (usage threshold vs account age).

maya: sure — short version: accounts created before 2024-09-01 get preserved rate for 90 days after rollout. Also any account with monthly spend > $5k gets an exemption review (manual). snippet:

```
grandfathering:
  created_before: "2024-09-01"
  preserve_duration_days: 90
  high_spend_threshold_usd: 5000
  manual_review_tag: "finance-exempt"
```

liam: That manual review flow needs a clear owner. Who triages? Last time it piled up and customers pinged support.

nisha: ops + finance will split. I'll take accounts tagged by billing-bot as high_spend for the first 48h. Can we add an automatic Slack alert when billing-bot flags >10 high-spend accounts in an hour?

billing-bot: auto: flagged 3 accounts as high_spend this morning (acct-2301, acct-8812, acct-4420). See /billing/ledger for details.

alex: Vendor side: our negotiated GPU discount schedule was updated — effective immediately per contract amendment. That lowers pass-through cost for the Dedicated tier by 6% but only for new invoices (can't retroactively apply). That changes modeled ARR and margin for the canary. Do we want to reflect that in price sheet v3 or keep v2 for canary to isolate variables?

sam: I'd prefer keeping v2 for the canary to avoid confounding the A/B signal. We can run a separate quick sensitivity check with the new vendor numbers, but don't flip production price yet.

maya: Agreed. Keep canary on v2 pricing. But we need to communicate to sales and SRE that vendor cost change is being tracked and will be applied in a controlled way. Alex, can you draft the short vendor note?

alex: Will do. Draft in #vendors in 15. Also thinking about invoice reconciliation: because vendor discount only applies to new invoices, we should ensure accounting marks which resources are covered. Liam, do you have capacity to add a csv export flag from the cost reconciliation job? Something like `vendor_tag=new-discount-2026-03` on rows?

liam: Yup, easy enough. I'll add a flag and a one-off report for the last 2 billing cycles. Expect PR within 2 hours.

nisha: For the grandfathering exceptions, what's the approval workflow? Slack thumbs + comment? formal Google form?

maya: For transparency, let's use a short Google form that populates a sheet and then trigger a pagerduty/Slack notification for reviewers. We want an audit trail for finance + sales. Form link I'll post after lunch.

sam: One more: A/B allocation. Current plan was 10% canary (v2) vs 90% baseline. If we see >3% revenue delta or >5% support tickets in canary, auto rollback. Is that still the rule?

maya: yes. I'll wire that into the rollout policy. Policy snippet for ops: 

```
rollout_policy:
  canary_pct: 10
  rollback_conditions:
    revenue_delta_pct: 3
    support_volume_delta_pct: 5
    monitoring_window_minutes: 60
```

billing-bot: alert: simulated revenue delta check at 09:12 shows +0.8% for canary window (10m sample). No action.

liam: Minor ask — make sure the metering change (we moved endpoint batching default) is in the rollout notes. That affects per-token cost and could skew canary revenue.

maya: Good catch. Add note: "batching default rollback to previous setting during canary" so we don't change metering variables.

alex: I'll send the vendor memo + reconciliation plan. Sam, please confirm you'll hold the canary pricing static. Nisha, you'll pick up manual reviews first 48h. Liam, PR for export flag. Maya will post the form and final cohort csv.

sam: Confirmed — holding canary pricing.

nisha: Confirmed — will monitor and triage.

liam: PR filed: https://git.redwood/infra/reports/pulls/462 — adds vendor_tag export and one-off CSV.

maya: Thanks team. Final step: anyone object to go/no-go at 11:30 PT? If no objections we'll flip the canary at 12:00 PT and watch metrics. :thumbsup: 

alex: :thumbsup: from vendor-side comms prep.

billing-bot: note: scheduled ledger snapshot at 11:55 PT for canary baseline.
